items.title: BoxBox: A Self-Hosted File Manager Without the Cloud Suite
items.summary: I spend quite a bit of time managing files on my servers, and I'm not always in the mood to fire up a terminal just to move something from one directory to another. Sure, SSH gets the job done, and I've got nothing against using the command line. But sometimes I'd rather open a browser, find what I'm looking for, and take care of it without remembering the exact path to a folder buried somewhere on the server. BoxBox is a self-hosted file manager built for that kind of everyday work. It gives you a modern web interface for browsing files already stored on your Linux server or NAS.

items.summary: It’s been one of the wettest Octobers on record in Phoenix, and Halloween was no outlier: for just the 12th time in recorded history, it rained on the holiday, according to the National Weather Service. items.title: The Medieval Villagers Who Fought for Their Freedom for 47 Years
items.summary: In 1179, the residents of a small French village began a legal battle against a powerful monastery over whether they were serfs. items.title: Planetary defense: How military and civil satellites are watching fireballs to help keep Earth safe from space rocks

items.title: On this day in space! Nov. 1, 1962: The Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 spacecraft to Red Planet during the Space Race
items.summary: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. While it did end up flying by Mars, the mission was not exactly a success. After it separated from the rocket, it deployed its solar panels and started cruising toward Mars. When mission controllers were checking out the telemetry it transmitted back to Earth, they found out that Mars 1 had sprung a leak in one of the gas valves that controls the spacecraft's orientation. And without a working orientation system, Mars 1 would have a hard time pointing its antennas in the right direction.

Saturday was the first Halloween with measurable rain in Phoenix since 1987, according to the National Weather Service. On Palmcroft Drive, in the historic Encanto-Palmcroft neighborhood, the weather forced some changes. Cookouts and parties moved under canopies, and umbrellas were plenty along the sidewalks. The street is a Halloween destination. Reeses put Palmcroft Drive on its 2026 Trick-or-Treatiest Street in America list, one of 150 streets in the country.

items.title: Irish and Estonian supermarkets also targeted in freezer cyber-hacks – Europe live
items.summary: Supermarkets across Europe have experienced temperature- control meddling The fake nuclear threats to Ukraine came as Russia resumed its attacks on the southern city of Kherson, just hours after the end of a ceasefire during which hundreds of people were evacuated from the nearby Kremlin-controlled town of Oleshky. Kherson’s military administration said a Russian drone hit a hospital at 7.40am. Video footage showed wrecked rooms, with windows blown out, doors broken, and debris on the street. Nobody was hurt, officials said.

items.title: Ultrathin kagome material opens a route to study unusual quantum states
items.summary: How atoms are arranged inside materials can influence the behavior of electrons and the resulting electronic states. Kagome lattices, repeating arrangements of atoms forming triangles that share corners (with hexagonal spaces between them), have been linked with the emergence of unusual electronic states.

items.title: UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years
items.summary: CASABLANCA, Morocco — The U.N.'s long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years, as a result of a U.S.-Russia standoff at U.N. headquarters over the territory's future. The end of the mission raises concerns about stability in the region. Rich in minerals and fisheries, Western Sahara is a vast desert territory roughly the size of Colorado along Africa's northwestern Atlantic coast. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.

items.title: Gag Order is a co-op, SCP-ish horror shooter about surviving as best you can against some nasty, tentacle covered cephalopod creatures
items.summary: What makes Carrion interesting obviously lies in playing as the monster in a horror game rather than being the one chased down by it. The game's nasty tentacle monster still gives me the heebie jeebies, so I really would hate to be hunted by one. This is where I point you towards Gag Order, a shooter where you are in fact hunted by a disgusting cephalopod creature all while tracking down a distress signal.

items.title: Marble Cognition raises $3.75M for its AI agent workers that watch and learn how people work
items.summary: Artificial intelligence agents have become two a penny in the enterprise today, but just because they’re rapidly being commoditized does not mean organizations know how best to use them. That’s the challenge a startup called Marble Cognition is trying to solve after raising $3.75 million in pre-seed funding to coincide with its launch today. The…

items.title: Swedish dietary surveys link higher ultraprocessed food intake to poorer nutrition
items.summary: A higher proportion of ultraprocessed food in the diet is generally associated with poorer dietary quality and, among adults, a somewhat higher prevalence of overweight and obesity. This is shown by a study that also critically examines the concept of ultraprocessed foods.

items.title: I imported a $2,000 electric truck from China. Five years later, here’s the truth
items.summary: Five years ago, I did something that seemed pretty ridiculous at the time. I bought a $2,000 electric mini-truck from China, had it shipped across the oceans to the US, and put it to work on my parents’ property in Florida. The little white mini electric truck became something of an internet sensation, with my original unboxing and testing video quickly racking up over 10 million views, plus several million more from the follow-up videos. It also attracted plenty of skeptics who were convinced that a $2,000 Chinese electric truck would fall apart within months, rust into oblivion, or otherwise prove to be a spectacular waste of money.

items.title: 2,700-year-old mummy head yields first molecular evidence linking aloe to Egyptian embalming
items.summary: What materials did ancient Egyptians use to preserve the dead, and how can their composition still be investigated thousands of years later? An interdisciplinary team at Marburg University has combined modern natural product analysis with Egyptology and the history of pharmacy to investigate these questions.

items.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
items.summary: Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff and confirmed airfares will be "materially higher" next summer because of a sharp rise in fuel costs following the US-Israel war with Iran. The airline said it expects fuel prices to remain high "well into 2027" unless there is a "swift resolution" to the conflict. Ryanair said its fuel bill is forecast to be â¬2bn (Â£1.6bn) higher in the short-term and its boss, Michael O'Leary, said airfares would have to rise by "double-digits" to help cover the cost.

items.title: An Underrated Stephen King Adaptation by the Best Director of His Work Is a Streaming Smash on HBO Max
items.summary: When it comes to Stephen King adaptations there are a few directors who just “get it.” From Mick Garris to Frank Darabont, there are certain directors that have taken King’s material and turned it into some of the best iterations put on screen. In recent years, a new director has found his way into King’s universe, and could end up being the best director to ever work on the horror master’s catalog of classics – especially when King himself says so.

items.title: OpenAI prepares lobbying blitz for a post-midterm Washington
items.summary: OpenAI is gearing up for a political lobbying and PR push after the US midterms. According to Axios, the company is bracing for a tougher fight in Washington if Democrats win control of the House. After two years under a friendly administration, big tech companies with close ties to President Trump are facing growing regulatory pressure. Rivals like Meta are already building bridges to Democrats. OpenAI's policy chief Chris Lehane plans to steer the AI debate through 2028 with a mix of new and repackaged proposals. The pitch centers on one idea: AI doesn't replace people. To back that up, OpenAI is proposing binding safety rules that build on earlier ideas. Lehane calls them "speed limits."

items.title: Hypertension or diabetes before pregnancy linked to higher risk of fetal heart defects
items.summary: Women with chronic hypertension (high blood pressure before pregnancy or diagnosed before 20 weeks of pregnancy) had a 30% higher risk of having a baby with critical congenital heart disease, the most severe form of heart defects, when compared to women with normal blood pressure before and during pregnancy, according to new independent, preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, held Nov. 6–9 in Chicago.

items.title: Cannabis use linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, especially strokes
items.summary: Cannabis use, including marijuana, appears to be linked with increased cardiovascular risk, especially for stroke, making it an important consideration for heart disease and stroke prevention and counseling, according to independent, new preliminary research to be presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026. The meeting is Nov. 6–9 in Chicago.

items.title: Hackers send fake nuclear threat alert to Ukraine emergency app
items.summary: Residents in Kyiv also warned of chemical attack and street-to-street fighting in false message sent by unknown party Europe live – latest updates Unknown hackers have targeted Ukraine’s nationwide emergency alert mobile app, sending residents in Kyiv a warning that they were at risk of an imminent nuclear strike. The app reported a high possibility of nuclear radiation late on Sunday. It also wrongly warned of a chemical threat to the Ukrainian capital and street-to-street fighting. The messages were written in English with spelling mistakes, as well as in Ukrainian.

items.title: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
items.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope still shines in the eyes of astronomers after 36 years in orbit, but it is not as nimble as it once was. Left alone, the observatory will plunge back into the atmosphere in the early-to-mid-2030s, closing the book on one of the most famous scientific instruments of the century. NASA last raised the orbit of Hubble in 2002, when the Space Shuttle Columbia visited the observatory for a servicing mission. The final shuttle servicing flight in 2009 did not reboost the telescope's orbit, and with the retirement of the shuttle fleet two years later, Hubble has steadily lost altitude with no way to stave off eventual destruction.

items.title: I'm 100% here for a more grounded, realistic GTA 6, one I believe won't come at the expense of its usual haphazard chaos
items.summary: Edge magazine unleashed a whopper of a 16-page feature all about Grand Theft Auto 6 earlier this week. After poring over every paragraph multiple times, one thing really stuck out to me: It feels like Rockstar is pushing for a more realistic, grounded experience. Those two words might sound like an absolute nightmare to some GTA aficionados. It's not like the series has never known how to be serious or gritty—see Grand Theft Auto 4—but it's always facilitated chaos with relative ease. Outlandish weapons, an easily gamed wanted system, NPCs that feel more like props to be mowed down than anything with a personality.

items.title: AI giants promise publishers new way to block some scraping
items.summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic pledged on Friday to give media outlets and other websites a single way to prevent their content from being scraped to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, amid growing criticisms and legal battles from news publishers.

items.title: Marriott posted earnings that beat expectations as U.S. hotel demand rose
items.summary: Marriott $MAR International reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $3.02 a share on Monday, up from $2.47 a year earlier, as hotel demand in the U.S. and Canada grew. That topped the $2.84 a share analysts expected, according to The Wall Street Journal. The average estimate in a separate analyst survey was $2.86 a share, according to The Associated Press. Reported net income rose 9% to $794 million, or $3.04 a share, from $728 million, or $2.67 a share, a year earlier. Revenue rose 8% to $7.005 billion.

items.title: From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence
items.summary: At a glance Evaluating Microsoft Copilot at enterprise scale requires test data that captures the full complexity of real organizations, yet real enterprise data contains sensitive information that cannot be used for evaluation under any circumstances. To resolve this tension, we built Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform: full-scale synthetic enterprise environments grounded in publicly available real-world data sources such as O*NET occupational data, online job postings, and SEC filings.

items.title: China state broadcaster pulls La Liga matches following Mbappé joke
items.summary: China Media Group had earlier demanded apologies from the three parties, calling them "an absolute prerequisite" for moving past the incident. It has acknowledged the apologies, but has not commented on how long the broadcast blackout will last. "My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," he had said. The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his having overseen one of the bloodiest chapters in the country's past.

items.title: The Bloodthirsty Bride Devours the King Manga Gets TV Anime in 2027
items.summary: A website opened on Monday to announce that a television anime of writer Shiki and artist Yū Shinonome's The Bloodthirsty Bride Devours the King (Chi ni Ueta Hanayome wa Ō o Kurau) manga will air next year. The "forbidden dark romantic fantasy" is set in an era of war. Kate, a princess maiden with vampiric powers, enters an arranged marriage with Luka, the mightiest king of the realm, to protect her motherland. However, on their first night, the scent of his blood awakens her true nature, which shakes their bond to the core.

items.title: November’s Bake Club Is a Triple Feature of Holiday Pies
items.summary: Is baking your entire personality? Is The Great British Baking Show your comfort watch? Or maybe you just love eating cookies? Either way, you’re one of us. Come join our Bon Appétit Bake Club. We’re Jesse and Shilpa, senior editors and the resident bakers of the Bon Appétit Test Kitchen. We love to bake—some might even call us obsessive—and we love to talk about all the hows and whys and what-didn’t-works that come with it. Think of the Bon Appétit Bake Club as a book club, but for baking. Each month we share a brand-new meticulously tested recipe.

items.title: Salted Coffee Custard Pie
items.summary: If you can’t be fussed with making coffee and dessert after a big holiday dinner, consider this twofer instead. The silky, sliceable, cool custard is rich and intense with two kinds of coffee, while the oatmeal crust is a tweedy-textured study in contrast. It’s prebaked to mitigate sogginess but doesn’t require pie weights. Mascarpone keeps the whipped cream firm and fluffy for a full 24 hours. Don’t be tempted to skip the cold-brew concentrate. You don’t want regular cold brew, and definitely not brewed and cooled coffee from your coffee machine at home, no matter how fancy.

items.title: Going to the gym just got easier for residents at this Paris homeless shelter
items.summary: At the nonprofit Emmaüs Solidarité homeless shelter in Paris, it’s not uncommon for new residents to have sleepless nights. But since the summer, residents have had a new way to cope with the stress of a restless evening: head to the courtyard and do a few circuits on their new outdoor gym. Through a partnership between the city, the nonprofit, and Omnigym, a Finnish fitness company, this new installation of outdoor exercise equipment seeks to not just help provide access to fitness gear, but build community and self-esteem.

items.title: Inside KFC’s big plan to win the chicken wars
items.summary: On a busy street in Dubai, there’s a building that’s impossible to miss. Its bright red facade glows with electric white lights. Three giant archways offer passersby a glimpse of a two-story screen playing constant editorial-style videos. Inside, a stark, almost brutalist construction is offset by two-tone red furniture and a neon wall mural. It’s not a club or a luxury store—it’s a KFC. We’re in the middle of a modern chicken war, and KFC wants to reclaim its icon status. Chicken—more specifically, the chicken tender—is undeniably having a moment, even as the rest of the fast-casual food space continues to languish in a post-pandemic, cost-of-living-induced slump.

items.title: Manor Lords becomes "Manure Lords" in a stinky new update for the medieval city builder
items.summary: A new Manor Lords update has arrived on the stable branch, and you might want to hold your nose before you dive in. Slavic Magic's medieval city builder has been testing quite a few new features on the beta branch in recent months, and a large set of those have now made their way into…

items.title: Judge says xAI must face NAACP lawsuit on data center pollution
items.summary: The legal battle revolves around the AI company’s operations in southern Memphis. A federal judge's latest ruling has denied xAI's request to dismiss a lawsuit that alleges its data center campus in Memphis, Tennessee is running turbines without proper permits and violating the Clean Air Act. The decision, from US District Judge Debra M. Brown, allows the lawsuit, which was filed by the NAACP, to move forward. The organization filed its legal action against xAI in April, accusing the company that's now known as SpaceXSI of using unpermitted methane gas turbines to power data centers in the Memphis area.

items.title: Tim Burton’s Iconic Gothic Fantasy Officially Becomes a Streaming Favorite
items.summary: The king of the gothic movie, Tim Burton, has teamed up with Johnny Depp on eight movies in total. One of their best, an adaptation of Washington Irving 's 1820 short story, "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow," is about to be reinvented through a feminist lens. Brought to life via the debut novel by filmmaker Lindsey Anderson Beer, Hollow has already assigned Sydney Sweeney to star as Katrina Van Tassel in the film, as she finds herself trapped in a love triangle between Brom Bones and Ichabod Crane.

items.title: Award‑winning Australian children’s author Craig Silvey jailed over child exploitation material
items.summary: Jasper Jones writer sent multiple messages about his sexual desire for young boys, Western Australian district court hears Warning: This article contains graphic content Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The award‑winning author Craig Silvey sent multiple messages about his sexual desire for young boys and was caught with explicit images of children and adults. The young adult novelist was jailed on Monday for seven months after pleading guilty to distributing and possessing child exploitation material earlier this year.

items.title: Tories accuse Shabana Mahmood of ‘U-turn’ on indefinite leave to remain policy – UK politics live
items.summary: Chris Philp says the home secretary is giving in to ‘open-borders Labour left’ ahead of an announcement this afternoon Downing Street has declined to say how much it cost for the plane carrying Andy Burnham and UK delegates to a Commonwealth leaders’ summit to stop in Manchester to pick him up (see 10.28am ), the Press Association reports. At the morning lobby briefing, asked if this was an appropriate use of public money, the PM’s spokesperson said: The prime minister’s travel arrangements are made on the basis of security, operational requirements, and value for money for the taxpayer.

items.title: Melting Ice in the Italian Dolomites Exposes Hundreds of World War I Munitions, Vestiges of the Vertiginous 'White War'
items.summary: High in the craggy peaks of northern Italy’s Dolomites, record-breaking summer heat has peeled back layers of ice and revealed troves of 20th-century weaponry. Over the course of the summer, the Italian army recovered and defused some 250 explosive devices dating back to World War I, according to ANSA, an Italian news agency. The dangerous relics surfaced across high-altitude slopes and melting glaciers in the Trentino-Alto Adige region. They were frequently spotted and reported by mountaineers and hikers.

items.title: China polysilicon prices hold amid market standoff, spot-futures gap
items.summary: The China Mono Premium, the OPIS assessment for mono-grade polysilicon used in n-type ingot production, was unchanged at CNY 38.786 ($5.82)/kg, or CNY 0.081/W, according to the OPIS Global Solar Markets Report released on Oct. 27. According to market participants, the fundamentals of the Chinese polysilicon market remain unchanged, with the market continuing to be characterized by manufacturers holding firm to full-cost-based offers while downstream buyers show limited willingness to accept current prices.

items.title: Power returns to the Grand Canyon’s South Rim
items.summary: GRAND CANYON NATIONAL PARK, AZ (AZFamily) — Power has returned to the Grand Canyon’s South Rim after severe weather moved through northern Arizona on Sunday. It was restored after several hours, according to the National Park Service. The exact cause of the outage is unclear. Park officials are asking visitors to delay travel to the area, use caution and monitor local weather alerts. The storms also sent floodwaters rising rapidly across the state, triggering water rescues and forcing evacuations in several Arizona communities.

items.title: datasette-llm 0.1a9
items.summary: Release: datasette-llm 0.1a9 I have some big upgrades to Datasette Agent in the pipeline, but in the meantime here's a tiny user experience improvement to the underlying datasette-llm plugin. It now picks up the default model used by LLM, which means you can start using Datasette Agent without needing to explicitly configure a default model: uvx --with datasette-agent datasette content.db --internal internal.db Previously you would also need to specify a model with -s plugins.datasette-agent.default_model gpt-6-astra. Tags: datasette, llm, datasette-agent…

items.title: What Wall Street is watching on election night: 9 sectors and the stocks tied to them
items.summary: Markets rarely treat a midterm election as the main event, but this year investors are positioning for a result most of them expect. CNBC reports that Wolfe Research calls a Democratic House the consensus base case and that 96% of the 138 investors it surveyed expect it. Fifty-eight percent of those investors expect Democrats to win the Senate, though Wolfe itself puts the odds at 49%. Prediction markets are more confident: Kalshi gives Democrats about a 90% chance of the House and 62% to 64% for the Senate, according to crypto outlets citing the platform, and Polymarket odds cited by Man Group put a Democratic sweep at 66% and a Republican sweep at just 8%.

items.title: Haley Stevens backs Mike Rogers. And, Gulf states brace for potential attack on Iran
items.summary: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens stunned the political landscape by endorsing GOP Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers for Michigan's open Senate seat, breaking with her party less than 48 hours before Election Day. The surprise defection followed weeks of deteriorating relations with her former primary opponent, Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed. In her endorsement of Rogers, Stevens cited El-Sayed's ties to political streamer Hasan Piker, whose remarks concerning Jewish people and Israel sparked backlash in August.

items.title: Al-Jawf becomes new hotspot in Yemen war between government forces, Houthis
items.summary: Al-Jawf has become a new focal point in the conflict between forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognised government and the Houthis, highlighting the strategic importance of the northern governorate. A major counteroffensive has been launched by the Yemeni government army and forces loyal to it to capture the strategic heights east of the provincial capital, al-Hazm, from the Houthis. The operations are part of Operation Dawn of Yemen, launched by the government last month to reverse Houthi territorial gains and restore state control in the country.

items.title: Iliana Yotova wins the presidential election in Bulgaria, portraying herself as the 'president of peace'
items.summary: "We are choosing between war and peace," Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev told voters ahead of Sunday's presidential election runoff between incumbent President Iliana Yotova, who opposes military aid to Ukraine and favors dialogue with Russia, and former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov, who is regarded as staunchly pro-European and pro-Ukrainian. With these words, it was clear that Sunday's runoff had turned into a kind of referendum on the country's foreign policy and stance on the war in Ukraine.

items.title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
items.summary: Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly two decades of military involvement in the country. Uganda's acting army spokesperson Chris Magezi on Monday said the first group of troops deployed to Somalia through a bilateral arrangement had already arrived back home and others would follow in a few days' time. He said all forces, including those under the African Union (AU) mission, would exit by the end of 2027 in the phased withdrawal. Uganda was the first African country to deploy troops to Somalia under the African Union Mission in Somalia (Amisom), which was established in 2007 to help protect the country's transitional government from attacks by Islamist militants.

items.title: NVIDIA Releases Auto Ontology: An Open Semantic Layer That Grounds AI Agent SQL
items.summary: NVIDIA has released Auto Ontology, an open library under the Apache 2.0 license. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is a semantic layer framework that builds a context layer from enterprise metadata. Agents use that layer to write SQL against certified business definitions. The repository states the problem plainly: a fast revenue answer is worthless if the number is wrong. TL;DR Library: Default LLM is nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b, with Nemotron embedding and reranking models. Runs on: Docker Compose for a local stack, or Kubernetes via Helm.

items.title: It's ACA open enrollment time. Here are the changes for health insurance shoppers
items.summary: Pennie, the ACA marketplace for Pennsylvania. She's pictured here in October 2025. ACA open enrollment runs from Nov. 1 through Jan. 15 in most states.'/> The ACA health insurance marketplaces — find yours at HealthCare.gov — open Nov. 1 for 2027 coverage. Getting an early start may be especially important this year.

items.title: BYD achieves over 300,000 BEV sales in a single month for the first time
items.summary: In October 2026, BYD sold over 300,000 pure electric vehicles in a single month for the first time. Globally, the Chinese manufacturer delivered over 490,000 vehicles, including plug-in hybrids. This represents an increase of around eleven per cent compared to October 2025.

items.title: A Pearl
items.summary: Writing to Robert Gathorne-Hardy in 1929, Logan Pearsall Smith referred to an account in the London Times of a solar eclipse as seen from Manila: The weather was cloudless, the conditions were perfect. Acacia trees closed their leaves as for the night; dew fell, chickens roosted, and the peasants in outlying villages, terrified by the awful phenomenon, supplicated the Saints. Smith wrote, “Could this sentence, which Flaubert might have written with the help of Gibbon, be the chance product of a journalist’s pen? I cannot think so.” For the record, a Times archivist attributed the passage to Willmott Lewis, who was Washington correspondent for the paper from 1920 to 1948.

items.title: Collective human metabolism produces 2 billion metric tons of CO₂ a year, global study estimates
items.summary: A University of Bath–led study has estimated that the carbon dioxide produced by humans as our bodies turn food into energy rose by 74% between 1985 and 2015, reaching 2.05 billion metric tons a year. Researchers say the findings could help scientists better understand where carbon comes from, where it goes and how human activity fits into the bigger picture.

items.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?
items.summary: People are peppering artificial intelligence chatbots everyday with questions, but when it comes to politics and the looming 2026 U.S. midterm elections, what role are AI platforms playing? Could an AI chatbot sway a voter to switch parties or re-examine their political beliefs? MIT researchers have built a new dashboard, called the LLM Election Observatory, to examine, in real-time, how popular AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 midterm elections.

items.title: Roman Coins Recovered in Hungary
items.summary: SOMOGY COUNTY, HUNGARY—More than 700 coins were discovered at three sites near the Drava River in southwestern Hungary by archaeologists from the Rippl-Rónai Museum, Hungary Today reports. Most of the coins have been dated to the rule of the emperor Constantine ( A.D. 307–337), but silver coins dating to the reigns of the emperors Antoninus Pius ( A.D. 138–161), Severus Alexander ( A.D. 222–235), Aurelian ( A.D. 270–275), and Probus ( A.D. 276–282) have also been identified. One coin, known as a “consecration coin,” is thought to have been minted to mark the death of Claudius II (reigned A.D.

items.title: Nearly 2,000 Boeing 737s Must Get Tail Inspections After Jets Pitched Up And Down Mid-Flight
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration has ordered inspections of nearly 2,000 Boeing 737 Next Generation (737NG) aircraft after multiple operators reported incidents in which the planes' noses moved up and down during flight. The airworthiness directive (AD) targets excessive movement in the hinges and jackscrew that support and move the aircraft's horizontal stabilizer.

items.title: Australia Repatriates Ancient Sculptures to China
items.summary: CANBERRA, AUSTRALIA— China Daily reports that Australian officials have repatriated the looted heads of two statues dating to the Northern Song Dynasty ( A.D. 960–1127) to China. The sculptures, which depict a civil official and a military official, were taken from imperial mausoleums near Kaifeng, the Song Dynasty capital in central China. Chinese Ambassador to Australia Liu Jinsong said that the statues once stood guard at ancient tombs—the civil official at the Yongchang Mausoleum and the military official at the Yongyu Mausolem.

items.title: Tomb Unearthed at Theater Site in Northwestern Turkey
items.summary: BURSA, TURKEY—According to a Türkiye Today report, a cremation tomb dated to the first century A.D. has been discovered among the 5,000 seats of a theater in the ancient city of Apollonia ad Rhyndacum, which is located in northwestern Turkey. The tomb was made up of a mudbrick chest covered by a gabled roof of terracotta tiles. “What was a tomb doing in a theater area when the city had its own necropolis?” asked Derya Şahin of Bursa Uludag University. “The grave must be a special one. It must carry some meaning, perhaps a trace of sacredness or heroism,” she reasoned.

items.title: Batteries Beat Norway’s Hydrogen Bulk Carriers on Cost in Two Modeled Routes
items.summary: Norwegian shipping company GMI Group is moving ahead with four hydrogen-electric bulk carriers for coastal freight. In October 2026, PowerCell confirmed a follow-up order that brings the program to 24 marine fuel-cell units with 5.4 MW of combined installed capacity. The first two ships, rated at 4,000 deadweight tonnes, are…

items.title: Chronicles: Medieval developer faces imminent closure after losing funding: 'What makes it hurt is how close we are. Early access is in reach'
items.summary: Chronicles: Medieval is an impressive looking open-world sandbox where players explore a dynamic Medieval world and fight in massive, authentic battles. It's been in development for more than four years and is due to launch into Steam early access early in 2027. However, there is a very real chance this will no longer happen, as developer Raw Power Games suddenly faces closure after funding for its game was pulled. On Friday, Raw Power Games posted a statement to Steam and on social media channels (via IGN ), explaining how the studio has suddenly found itself in dire straits.

items.title: Martian Polar Crater Ice Shifts with Seasonal Frost
items.summary: The planet Mars shares many landforms and weather patterns with the Earth, including changing seasons, volcanoes, canyons, dust storms and dust devils, and water ice. But one feature that Earth and Mars share among the eight planets in our solar system are polar ice caps. Both are one of each planet’s striking features, but the major difference is while Earth’s polar ice caps are both comprised of water, Mars’ north polar ice cap is only comprised of water while its southern polar ice cap is carbon dioxide.

items.title: Sudan files complaints against Ethiopia with UN over deadly drone spree
items.summary: Sudan has lodged a complaint against Ethiopia with both the United Nations Security Council and the African Union’s Peace and Security Council after a series of deadly drone attacks this year. In a statement late on Sunday, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary group of using Ethiopian territory to launch “brazen aggression” against “civilian sites and power stations” in Sudan, resulting in hundreds of casualties and disruptions to essential services.

items.title: As aid situation worsens, displaced Sudanese worry about warnings of famine
items.summary: The sound of gunfire forced 50-year-old Aisha Adam to flee her home in the al-Kalakla neighbourhood of Khartoum days after war erupted in Sudan between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on April 15, 2023. She went to the neighbouring city of Omdurman, but fighting followed her and in May 2023, Adam had to find a new refuge. It brought her to a camp for internally displaced people (IDPs) in Port Sudan, on the country’s Red Sea coast, where she lives with her orphaned grandson and nephew.

items.title: Southwest’s 737 MAX 7 Targets March 2027 Launch With 150 Seats and Starlink
items.summary: DALLAS- Southwest Airlines (WN) plans to start Boeing 737 MAX 7 passenger flights in March 2027, according to an internal rollout document. The jets will have 150 Recaro seats, Starlink internet, seat power, and larger overhead bins. Deliveries begin in mid-to-late December, with preparation work at Paine Field (PAE), Phoenix (PHX) and Kansas City (MCI). The first 27 aircraft will take over overwater flying, including Burbank (BUR) to Honolulu (HNL). Southwest Outlines Path to MAX 7 Passenger Service The Boeing 737 MAX 7 received FAA certification on August 3, 2026, after years of delays.

items.title: Eli teases the launch of a much faster electric microcar
items.summary: Eli Electric Vehicles is getting ready to reveal a new version of its tiny electric microcar, and this one could expand its usefulness beyond the slow lane. items.title: Poles Apart
items.summary: A circle is divided by points into 3 k arcs such that there are k arcs each of length 1, 2, and 3. Prove that two of the division points are diametrically opposite one another. Suppose that this is not the case, that none of the division points are diametrically opposite one another. This means that every arc of length 1 must stand opposite an arc of length 3. Remove one such pair, an arc of length 1 and its opposing arc of length 3. Now we’ve divided the circle into two large arcs. If one of these large arcs contains m arcs of length 1 and n arcs of length 3, then the other contains n arcs of length 1 and m arcs of length 3.

items.title: ‘REANIMAL’, ‘Resident Evil Requiem’ Lead Nominations for The Horror Game Awards 2026
items.summary: Horror gamers ate well this year, but the battle for which game was on top happens next month with the 2026 edition of The Horror Game Awards, which will take place on November 20 from 26 Leake Street in London, UK. Over 100 titles compete in 21 categories (seriously) this year, with ten games this year having at least five nominations. items.title: 8 Cozy Vrbos & Airbnbs in Manchester-by-the-Sea, Massachusetts
items.summary: Less than fifty miles north of Boston waits one of New England’s quaintest small towns: Manchester-by-the-Sea, Massachusetts. The town sits on the coast of Cape Ann, which is known for its stretching, sandy beaches and scenic outlooks. (One of them, Singing Beach, even squeaks when you walk on the sand.) Along the coast, you can also find dozens of grand mansions that were built by affluent visitors over the last century. The small town is home to less than six thousand residents, but the area comes alive during summer as families pack into the seaside town.

items.title: How to build an air purifier in 6 simple steps
items.summary: Though invisible itself, the air we breathe is a microcosm of identifiable pollen, fungal spores, viruses, dust particles, and fine particles of human pollution from everything from cars to asphalt sidewalks. It’s not something we should obsess over day to day, but as more people measure air quality on their own, many are getting readings they’d prefer to address. However, not everyone wants to buy an air purifier, which can cost several hundred dollars. One proposed solution for at-home air filtration is to use readily available materials like cardboard, box fans, square HVAC filters, and everyone’s favorite building material: duct tape.

items.title: Update: American Airlines Pilots Union Retracts Warning Not To Eat Dessert
items.summary: Aviation watchdog JonNYC shares the warning from the Allied Pilots Association’s Aeromedical–HIMS Committee. It covers crews based in or transiting Phoenix, where the contracted caterer has put the dessert on some crew meal trays. The contracted catering provider has included tiramisu containing alcohol on some crew meal trays. Because the dessert is not cooked after the alcohol is added, alcohol may remain in the finished product. The committee says it’s working with the Phoenix Flight Office to have the item removed and replaced.

items.title: Come for the Skiing, Stay for the Caviar: What’s New in Food at North American Ski Resorts
items.summary: Every winter, ski resorts across North America tout their latest multimillion-dollar upgrades: new lodges, high-tech snowmaking systems, and chairlifts that get you to the summit in record time. But sometimes, the best part of a ski trip isn’t the skiing. It’s the bowl of ramen that warms you up after a freezing morning, the mid-mountain après-ski party where you find yourself belting out ’80s rock songs with strangers, and the unexpectedly delicious waffle at the summit that takes an already great ski vacation from a nine to a 10.

items.title: Radomes: Why Their Colors Often Didn’t Match The Aircraft
items.summary: Often coated in black in earlier years, aircraft radomes frequently differed in color from the rest of the aircraft, creating visible contrasts between panels and sections. The concepts of RADAR (Radio Detection and Ranging) were developed in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, but it was during the World War II years that it emerged as a practical tool, with the ground-based version proving its value during the Battle of Britain. The technology also found its way into aircraft for detecting ships and other aircraft, leading to the need for aerodynamic protective coverings for the antennas.

items.title: 10 Waterfront Airbnbs on the Oregon Coast with Stunning Pacific Ocean Views
items.summary: Looking for solitude, rugged views, and plenty of space to roam? So long as you aren’t afraid of a little fog and cold, the Oregon Coast should be high on your bucket list. The state has over 350 miles of coast, ranging from sandy beaches to rocky cliff faces. The coastline is also home to six wildlife refuges, ensuring you won’t run into overdeveloped beachfront areas, and is home to small towns galore. In fact, Oregon maintains a fully accessible coastline thanks to the Oregon Beach Bill, which prevents the privatization of its beaches from the vegetation line to the Pacific Ocean.

items.title: Straw, Squeeze or Gravity? How to Choose the Right Water Filter for Your Adventure
items.summary: Portable water filters come in a lot of shapes and sizes, from ultralight straws you can tuck into a daypack to gravity systems capable of supplying water for an entire campsite. The good news: choosing one doesn’t have to be complicated. The right setup mostly comes down to how you plan to use it. A solo hiker stopping at streams along the trail has very different needs than a family filtering several liters for drinking, cooking and coffee at camp. So before comparing weights, capacities and technical specs, start with a simpler question: What will your adventure actually look like?
